hypothesis: A state-conditioned five-row prefix that is dead under sampled sixth-row branching may still admit a compatible pair of final rows; exact two-row completion at every visited depth-five prefix will expose such a witness if the first-five search reaches its neighborhood.
rationale: The prior on-demand search reached depth six on two seeds, but exact completion of those saved six-row states found no seventh row. The remaining uncertainty is whether the sixth-row sampler discarded the right sixth-row branch. Enumerating all compatible rows for the final two positions and checking pairwise disjointness directly attacks that uncertainty while retaining state-conditioned generation for the first five rows.
expected_information_gain: A verified seven-row assignment is target progress. A large number of exact final-row candidates with no disjoint pairs quantifies the pair bottleneck. A bounded search with no pair closes this two-row completion policy and requires a broader multi-row or structural mechanism; no finite outcome implies global infeasibility.
method: Run the existing state-conditioned DFS for three fixed seeds with exact-pair mode enabled. At depth five, form the forbidden mask from all used and explicitly gapped differences, exhaustively enumerate increasing normalized six-mark rows under scope 111 up to a 30000-node per-prefix budget, and test every unordered pair for disjoint difference masks. Preserve the deepest partial state and independently validate any seven-row output with research_tools/verify_dts_independent.py.
metric: target reach, deepest sampled prefix, DFS nodes, incremental generator nodes, exact-completion nodes, exact compatible final rows, pair checks, generated rows, and elapsed time per seed
metric_relation_to_true_objective: Only a complete seven-row assignment accepted by the independent integer verifier is a scope<=111 true-objective witness. Exact final-row counts and prefix depth are finite search evidence only.

compute_budget.cpu: one native C++ process per seed, sequential
compute_budget.memory_intent: bounded final-row vector per depth-five prefix and two-word masks

kill_condition: Stop a seed at 60 seconds, 100000 DFS nodes, or a complete independently validated witness; cap each depth-five exact completion at 30000 enumeration nodes; stop after the three declared seeds. Do not infer infeasibility from these finite prefixes or budgets.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if complete and validator-valid

previous_best_comparison.saved_six_row_completion: zero compatible seventh rows in two exact checks
previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: replace sampled sixth/seventh branching with exact pair completion after the same five-row state-conditioned prefix search

interpretation: The exact-pair policy reached only depth-five prefixes on all three declared seeds because terminal pair enumeration consumed the wall budget. It found 8, 4, and 4 compatible final rows respectively, with 4, 2, and 6 pair checks and no disjoint pair. The saved five-row prefixes independently audit to 75 unique differences each. This is finite methodological evidence only.
what_was_learned: Making the last two rows exact removes terminal sampling uncertainty, but it sharply reduces prefix throughput and did not reveal a completion in the visited branches. The current state-conditioned DFS plus exact-pair policy is therefore not a productive witness route within the declared budget.
recommended_next_action: Close this pair-completion policy. Do not increase the same terminal budget or repeat the same prefix search; any continuation must change the multi-row exploration mechanism or use a new structural construction hypothesis.
repetition_justification: This changes the terminal search operation from sampled row generation to exhaustive two-row completion over each visited depth-five prefix; it is not a seed or budget repeat of dts-ondemand-constrained-001.
